SI base units (7)

QuantityUnit
Lengthmetre (m)
Masskilogram (kg)
Timesecond (s)
Electric currentampere (A)
Temperaturekelvin (K)

Supplementary: radian (plane angle), steradian (solid angle) — both dimensionless.

Dimensional formulas you must know

Force$[MLT^{-2}]$Pressure, stress, Young's modulus, energy density$[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$
Work, energy, torque, heat$[ML^2T^{-2}]$Power$[ML^2T^{-3}]$
Momentum, impulse$[MLT^{-1}]$Angular momentum, Planck's constant$[ML^2T^{-1}]$
Coefficient of viscosity$[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$Surface tension, spring constant$[MT^{-2}]$
Gravitational constant $G$$[M^{-1}L^3T^{-2}]$Universal gas constant $R$$[ML^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]$
Charge$[AT]$Potential / EMF$[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}]$
Resistance$[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}]$Capacitance$[M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2]$

Dimensionless quantities

Strain, refractive index, relative density, angle, Poisson's ratio, coefficient of friction, all trigonometric and exponential arguments.

Errors

  • Absolute error $\Delta a_i = |a_{mean} - a_i|$; relative error $= \Delta a_{mean}/a_{mean}$; percentage error $= $ relative error $\times 100$.
  • Sum/difference: absolute errors add. Product/quotient: relative (percentage) errors add.
  • If $Z = A^p B^q / C^r$: $\dfrac{\Delta Z}{Z} = p\dfrac{\Delta A}{A} + q\dfrac{\Delta B}{B} + r\dfrac{\Delta C}{C}$.

Significant figures

  • All non-zero digits are significant. Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
  • Leading zeros are never significant (0.0052 → 2 s.f.). Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant (5.200 → 4 s.f.).
  • Rounding: if the dropped digit is 5 exactly, round to make the preceding digit even (2.745 → 2.74, 2.735 → 2.74).
  • Addition/subtraction: result keeps the least number of decimal places. Multiplication/division: least number of significant figures.

Instruments

  • Least count of vernier = 1 MSD − 1 VSD (commonly 0.01 cm). Screw gauge L.C. = pitch / number of circular divisions.

Exam tip

KCET asks 1–2 questions here every year: usually 'which pair has the same dimensions', a percentage-error calculation, or dimensions of a constant from an equation. Learn the table above by heart.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of Planck's constant is
questions.explanation: $E = h\nu \Rightarrow h = E/\nu = [ML^2T^{-2}]/[T^{-1}] = [ML^2T^{-1}]$. Same as angular momentum.
questions.tip: Planck's constant and angular momentum share dimensions — a favourite KCET question.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs has the same dimensions?
questions.explanation: Work $= F\cdot d$ and torque $= F\times r$ are both $[ML^2T^{-2}]$. Pressure is force per area, power is energy per time.

questions.q: The number of significant figures in $0.005080$ is
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. 5, 0, 8 and the trailing 0 after the decimal are significant → 4.

questions.q: The percentage errors in the measurement of mass and speed are 2% and 3% respectively. The maximum error in the estimate of kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: $K = \tfrac12 mv^2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta K}{K} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta v}{v} = 2\% + 2(3\%) = 8\%$.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity is
questions.explanation: From Stokes' law $F = 6\pi\eta r v$: $\eta = F/(rv) = [MLT^{-2}]/([L][LT^{-1}]) = [ML^{-1}T^{-1}]$.

questions.q: Which physical quantity has the dimensional formula $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = $[MLT^{-2}]/[L^2] = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$. Stress, Young's modulus and energy density share this.

questions.q: A screw gauge has a pitch of 1 mm and 100 divisions on its circular scale. Its least count is
questions.explanation: Least count = pitch / number of circular divisions = 1 mm/100 = 0.01 mm.

questions.q: One newton is equal to
questions.explanation: $1\,\text{N} = 1\,\text{kg m s}^{-2} = 10^3\,\text{g}\times 10^2\,\text{cm s}^{-2} = 10^5$ dyne.

questions.q: If velocity $v$, acceleration $a$ and force $F$ are taken as fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of mass is
questions.explanation: $F = ma \Rightarrow m = F/a = [F a^{-1}]$. Velocity does not enter.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a dimensionless quantity?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity has dimensions $[T^{-1}]$ (rad s$^{-1}$; the radian is dimensionless). The others are ratios of like quantities.

questions.q: The value 2.745 rounded off to three significant figures is
questions.explanation: When the digit to be dropped is exactly 5, the preceding digit is left unchanged if it is even: 2.745 → 2.74. (2.735 would also become 2.74.)

questions.q: The dimensions of $\dfrac{a}{b}$ in the equation $P = \dfrac{a - t^2}{bx}$, where $P$ is pressure, $x$ is distance and $t$ is time, are
questions.tip: Only like quantities can be added: $a$ must have dimensions of $t^2$.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of the universal gravitational constant $G$ is
A physical quantity $X = \dfrac{A^2 B^{1/2}}{C^{1/3} D^3}$. The percentage errors in $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ are 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% respectively. The percentage error in $X$ is
The SI unit of luminous intensity is
questions.explanation: Candela (cd) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity; lumen and lux are derived units of luminous flux and illuminance.

questions.q: A light year is a unit of
questions.explanation: A light year is the distance light travels in vacuum in one year (about $9.46\times10^{15}$ m), despite the word 'year'.

questions.q: The order of magnitude of the mass of an electron ($9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg) is
questions.explanation: Since the coefficient 9.1 is greater than 5, the power is rounded up: order of magnitude $= 10^{-31+1} = 10^{-30}$ kg.

questions.q: The product $4.2 \times 1.15$, expressed to the correct number of significant figures, is
questions.explanation: $4.2\times1.15 = 4.83$, but 4.2 has only 2 significant figures, so the result must be rounded to 2 s.f.: 4.8.

questions.q: Two lengths are measured as $a = (5.0 \pm 0.2)$ cm and $b = (3.0 \pm 0.1)$ cm. The value of $a - b$ with its absolute error is
questions.explanation: For subtraction, absolute errors add: $a-b = 2.0$ cm and $\Delta(a-b) = \Delta a + \Delta b = 0.2+0.1 = 0.3$ cm.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of specific heat capacity (in $Q = mc\Delta T$) is
questions.explanation: $c = Q/(m\Delta T) = [ML^2T^{-2}]/([M][K]) = [L^2T^{-2}K^{-1}]$; the mass cancels out.

questions.q: For a fluid of density $\rho$ flowing with velocity $v$ through a pipe of diameter $d$ and viscosity $\eta$, which combination is dimensionless (the Reynolds number)?
questions.explanation: $[\rho vd/\eta] = \dfrac{[ML^{-3}][LT^{-1}][L]}{[ML^{-1}T^{-1}]} = [M^0L^0T^0]$, so Reynolds number $= \rho vd/\eta$ is dimensionless.

questions.q: If, with the jaws of a vernier caliper fully closed, the vernier zero lies to the right of the main scale zero, this is called a
questions.explanation: When the vernier zero is displaced to the right (positive side) of the main scale zero on closing the jaws, it is a positive zero error, and this reading must be subtracted from all measurements.

questions.q: A screw gauge has pitch 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale, with a positive zero error of 0.02 mm. While measuring a wire, the main scale reads 3 mm and the circular scale reads 20 divisions. The true diameter of the wire is
questions.explanation: L.C. $= 0.5/50 = 0.01$ mm. Observed reading $= 3 + 20\times0.01 = 3.20$ mm. True reading $=$ observed $-$ zero error $= 3.20 - 0.02 = 3.18$ mm.

questions.q: Using dimensional analysis, the time period of a simple pendulum of length $l$ in a gravitational field $g$ must be proportional to
questions.explanation: Only $\sqrt{l/g}$ has the dimension $[T]$: $[L/(LT^{-2})]^{1/2} = [T^2]^{1/2} = [T]$, consistent with $T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$.

questions.q: A car moves at 72 km/h. Its speed in m/s is
questions.explanation: $72\,\text{km/h} = 72\times\dfrac{5}{18}\,\text{m/s} = 20\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.q: The SI unit of pressure is the
questions.explanation: Pressure $=$ force/area, with SI unit pascal (Pa) $=$ N/m$^2$; newton, joule and watt are units of force, energy and power respectively.

questions.q: The parallax method is used in astronomy chiefly to measure the
questions.explanation: By observing the apparent shift (parallax angle) of a nearby star against distant background stars from two positions of Earth's orbit, its distance can be calculated.

questions.q: Which statement correctly expresses the principle of homogeneity of dimensions?
options: An equation that is dimensionally correct is always physically correct
Dimensional formulas can be used to find numerical proportionality constants
Only quantities with the same dimensions can be added, subtracted or equated
All quantities in an equation must have different dimensions
questions.explanation: The principle of homogeneity states that terms being added, subtracted or equated in a valid physical equation must all have the same dimensions; dimensional analysis cannot fix dimensionless constants or guarantee physical correctness.

questions.q: In an experiment, $R = V/I$ where $V = (100 \pm 5)$ V and $I = (10 \pm 0.2)$ A. The percentage error in $R$ is
questions.explanation: For division, percentage errors add: $\dfrac{\Delta R}{R}\times100 = \dfrac{5}{100}\times100 + \dfrac{0.2}{10}\times100 = 5\% + 2\% = 7\%$.

questions.q: Which of the following is an SI base unit, not a derived unit?
questions.explanation: Mole is one of the seven SI base units (amount of substance); newton, joule and watt are all derived from the base units.

questions.q: Angular momentum has the same dimensional formula as
questions.explanation: Both angular momentum and Planck's constant have dimensions $[ML^2T^{-1}]$, while torque and work share $[ML^2T^{-2}]$ and power is $[ML^2T^{-3}]$.

questions.q: The sum $4.237 + 3.2$, expressed to the correct number of decimal places, is
questions.explanation: $4.237+3.2=7.437$, but for addition the result keeps only as many decimal places as the least precise term (3.2 has 1 decimal place), giving 7.4.

questions.q: From the force on a current-carrying conductor $F = BIL$, the dimensional formula of magnetic field $B$ is
On a vernier caliper, 1 main scale division (MSD) is 1 mm and 10 vernier scale divisions (VSD) coincide with 9 MSD. The least count of the instrument is
questions.explanation: 1 VSD $= 0.9$ MSD $= 0.9$ mm. Least count $= 1$ MSD $-$ 1 VSD $= 1 - 0.9 = 0.1$ mm.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a systematic error?
options: An observer's careless mistake made in a single reading
Statistical error that reduces on averaging many readings
Random error due to unpredictable fluctuations in conditions
Zero error of the measuring instrument
questions.explanation: A zero error is reproducible in every reading (a systematic error) and can be corrected for, unlike random errors, which fluctuate unpredictably and are reduced by averaging.

questions.q: The time period $T$ of oscillation of a small liquid drop of radius $r$, density $\rho$, held together by surface tension $S$, is found using dimensional analysis to be proportional to
questions.explanation: Writing $T \propto \rho^a r^b S^c$ and matching $[M^0L^0T^1]$ with $[\rho]=[ML^{-3}]$, $[r]=[L]$, $[S]=[MT^{-2}]$ gives $a=\tfrac12$, $b=\tfrac32$, $c=-\tfrac12$, so $T \propto \sqrt{\rho r^3/S}$.

questions.q: The SI unit of frequency is the
questions.explanation: Frequency has dimension $[T^{-1}]$ and SI unit hertz (Hz) $= $ s$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities has the same dimensional formula as impulse?
questions.explanation: Impulse $= F\Delta t$ has dimension $[MLT^{-1}]$, identical to momentum $mv$; by the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse equals the change in momentum.

questions.q: A quantity $X = \dfrac{A^3B^2}{C\sqrt{D}}$. If the percentage errors in $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ are 2%, 1%, 3% and 4% respectively, the percentage error in $X$ is
The number of significant figures in $6.020\times10^{23}$ is
questions.explanation: In the coefficient 6.020, all digits — including the trailing zero after the decimal point — are significant, giving 4 significant figures.
